Three Lords scrutiny graphs

Built 2026-05-27 from UK Parliament APIs, Lords RMFI, the APPG register cache and Lords written questions. Each graph is an RDF (N-Quads) dump plus a queryable example HTML.

1. Scrutiny graph — Act → enabling power → SI → laying department → Lords division → peers → interests

40 most-recent Lords divisions on statutory-instrument motions, joined with each SI's enabling Act and laying department, the four scrutiny committees, and every peer's voting record + declared sectoral interests.

  • → Report (HTML)
  • N-Quads · manifest.json

9 example queries answered: dept-by-division-count, Acts generating most Lords-visible SIs, AI-tagged peers voting on SIs, scrutiny-committee membership, etc.

2. Transparency graph — Lords interests × APPG officers / secretariats / funders

Entity-resolution overlap between the APPG register and the Lords RMFI. Framed as context, not allegation. Surfaces named-entity matches where the same organisation appears as an APPG secretariat / benefit-provider and in a peer's declared interest text.

  • → Report (HTML)
  • N-Quads · manifest.json

5 officer-self-overlaps surfaced; Google → PICTFOR & Lord Vaizey; National Grid → Environment APPG & Lord Livingston; etc. Skipped Companies House (no API key) and ORCL lobbying register (Salesforce 403).

3. Accountability graph — Lords question → answer → arm's-length body

5,000 most-recent Lords written questions (Nov 2025 → May 2026) joined with their answering body, asker, and any named arm's-length body / regulator / agency mentioned in the answer text. Captures follow-up question chains via HLnnnnn references.

  • → Report (HTML)
  • N-Quads · manifest.json

NHS England (134 mentions, 3 depts), MOD (38, 6 depts), Ofcom (24, 4 depts) lead the indirect-accountability list. Lord Kamall is the most frequent NHS-England pursuer; Lord Jackson of Peterborough chains the most follow-up questions.

How to query locally

All three graphs are N-Quads. Spin up a SPARQL endpoint over any of them with the repo's local-sparql skill:

parl local-sparql up third_party/data/scrutiny-graph/scrutiny.nq
parl local-sparql up third_party/data/transparency-graph/transparency.nq
parl local-sparql up third_party/data/accountability-graph/accountability.nq

Or load all three together for cross-graph queries. The example queries are in tmp/*-graph/queries.py.
